content:
I want a small app for keeping track of the books I'm reading.

When I open it I want to see what I'm currently reading and what I've finished. I want to add a book from a form, mark one as finished, and click through to a book to see its title, author and my notes. I'd like to be able to send someone a link to a single book.

Nothing fancy and no accounts. Skip the database, save the books to a JSON file so they're still there after a restart.

Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. echo '--- mark finished ---' && \
ID1=${LOC1##*/} && \
curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code} -> %{redirect_url}\n' -X POST "http://localhost:3000/books/$ID1/finish" && \

kill $(cat /tmp/server.pid) && sleep 0.3 && (node server.mjs &>/tmp/server.log & echo $! > /tmp/server.pid) && sleep 1 && \
curl -s http://localhost:3000/ | grep -cE 'Dune|Piranesi'

content.text:
Done. Run it with `npm start` and open http://localhost:3000.

It's a zero-dependency Node app — no framework, no database, no accounts:

- **`server.mjs`** — the HTTP server and server-rendered pages. The home page shows "Currently reading" and "Finished" sections plus an add-book form (title, author, notes). Each book has a "Finished it" button and links to its own page.
- **`lib/store.mjs`** — the storage layer. Books live in `data/books.json` (created on first add, gitignored), written atomically via a temp-file rename so a crash can't corrupt it.
- **Shareable links** — each book gets a permanent URL like `/book/<id>`, rendered entirely server-side, so anyone you send it to sees the title, author, and notes with no setup.

I verified the full flow end-to-end with the running server: adding books redirects to the book page, marking finished moves a book to the Finished section with the date, unknown ids return 404, empty title/author is rejected with a 400, HTML in notes is escaped, and books survive a server restart. There are also 5 vitest tests covering the store (`npm test`), all passing.

One thing to know: since there are no accounts, anyone who can reach the server can see and edit the list — fine on your own machine; if you ever host it publicly you'd want to add some protection.
